transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam Ortega (Redwood SE); Priya Kapoor (Stillwater Head of MLOps); Jon Mercer (Stillwater Director of Platform); Sara Nunez (Stillwater Procurement)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Renewal conversation focused on adding reserved capacity and expanding to EU + APAC private/VPC options; customer wants pilot in EU first.
- Key asks: latency SLOs for their top workloads, audit logs/KMS details, amended pricing for 12-month committed plan with burst capacity.
- Next steps: pricing worksheet, benchmark results, security artifact exchange, schedule pilot kickoff.

Topics:
- Capacity uplift options (reserved capacity tiers, burst)
- Private/VPC onboarding timeline for EU and APAC
- Security/compliance (KMS, SOC2, audit logs, SSO)
- Benchmarks: tail latency vs cost tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh, happy Friday. Maya from Redwood here, with Liam on the line as well.
[00:00:12] Priya: Thanks Maya. We, we have about 50 minutes, I think, and wanted to focus on the retainer uplift and the EU pilot path.
[00:00:20] Jon: Yep and also clarify the KMS/HSM approach — we have a vendor we prefer, and network topology for VPC is key.
[00:00:29] Liam: Great, yeah, we'll cover the infra bits. Quick agenda: pricing options, pilot plan, security and benchmarks. Sound ok?
[00:00:37] Priya: Sounds good.
[00:00:39] Maya: Cool. To start, can you share current usage profile? Token volumes, peak qps, and the prompt families you want us to benchmark?
[00:00:48] Priya: Sure. Right now average token volume is around 120M tokens per month, peaks on the 1st qtr microservice are about 480 qps for short-context prompts, long-context doc-summarization runs are fewer but heavy — those are our cost drivers.
[00:01:03] Jon: And importantly, we have two priority workloads: 1) chat-like low-latency inference for customer UX (latency target 120 ms p50 ideally), and 2) batch document summarization with 8k to 32k context length where throughput matters more than latency.
[00:01:20] Maya: Got it. That's helpful. For the low-latency profile, reserved dedicated capacity tends to bring predictable tail latency; hosted is cheaper for base but has more variance.
[00:01:31] Priya: Right and we've been weighing cost vs p95 tail — last month saw p95 spikes that impacted UX.
[00:01:37] Liam: If I can jump in, we usually recommend a mixed strategy — reserved pool for the latency-sensitive endpoint and hosted fallback for overflow, plus prefix/KV cache for chat to reduce per-token cost.
[00:01:49] Jon: Quick question — does the prefix cache work across variants? We run model variants for A/B testing.
[00:01:55] Liam: Yes, but with caveats — cache keying needs to be consistent. Also note, the KV cache is per-model-variant; mis-keying means misses. Sorry, my voice: K-V cake — I mean K-V cache — transcription, ha.
[00:02:07] Priya: (laughs) noted.
[00:02:09] Maya: On pricing, we prepared two reserved tiers — a 12-month commit and a 3-month staging ramp. The 12-month has best unit economics and includes burst credits. We'll send the worksheet.
[00:02:20] Sara: Procurement will need the contract redline and PO path. For the 12-month, do you have cancellation or step-down clauses? We typically need a 30-day notice on scale changes.
[00:02:32] Maya: Yes, we can include a step-down provision with a 30–60 day notice and pro-rata adjustments. We'll include that in the amendment.
[00:02:39] Jon: On the EU pilot — timeline questions. We want private VPC in eu-west-1 for now, with KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. What's realistic?
[00:02:51] Liam: For EU private VPC, typical onboarding cycle is 4–6 weeks once networking and KMS details are confirmed. If you want on-prem, that adds time. We can stage with dedicated small pool for pilot.
[00:03:06] Priya: 4–6 weeks is okay. For KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault + cloud KMS; HSM-backed keys preferred for production. Do you support customer-managed CMKs?
[00:03:16] Liam: Yes, we support CMKs and HSM integrations, and we can point logs to your collector. We'll need the KMS vendor and IAM roles.
[00:03:23] Priya: We'll share a vendor contact and an architecture doc.
[00:03:27] Maya: Great. Also, SOC2 and ISO — we have the artifacts; shall I share the security pack and SOC2 report link?
[00:03:34] Jon: Yes please. Also MFA for Redwood console and SSO via SAML for our admins.
[00:03:40] Maya: SAML SSO and RBAC are standard — we'll send the SSO metadata and RBAC map.
[00:03:45] Sara: For procurement timeline, target is signing by end of year if pricing and security checks align. Our finance team wants a 30-day invoice term. Is Net30 supportable?
[00:03:54] Maya: Net30 is fine for enterprise customers; we'll check the amendment but that's standard.
[00:03:59] Priya: Back to benchmarks — can you run tail-latency tests with our sample prompts for the dedicated pool? We want end-to-end numbers including tokenization and streaming overhead.
[00:04:12] Liam: Yes — we'll do dedicated vs hosted comparisons and include p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. We'll run the tests over 24 hours to catch burst patterns.
[00:04:22] Priya: If you could include the KV cache on the chat ones, that'd be great.
[00:04:25] Liam: Yep, test matrix will include cache/no-cache and with different batch sizes.
[00:04:30] Jon: A question on fallbacks: if the dedicated pool is saturated and fails over to hosted, do you preserve latency SLOs or is there a degradation plan? We need deterministic behavior for our SLAs.
[00:04:41] Maya: We provide routed fallback policies — we can set a hard cutoff and a soft cutoff. Soft overflow keeps accepting but with degraded SLOs; hard cutoff rejects. We'll align policy to your SLA.
[00:04:52] Jon: Good. Please document the failover behavior and expected tail latencies in the bench report.
[00:04:58] Maya: Will do.
[00:05:01] Priya: Security review — can we set a review session with your security engineer? We want to deep-dive encryption key lifecycle, audit log fields, and data retention.
[00:05:10] Liam: Absolutely. I'll invite our security lead, but I can cover KMS and logging basics now. For audit logs we include request id, model version, redwood-token-id, timestamps, and anonymized prompt hashing per your config.
[00:05:25] Priya: Anonymized prompt hashing — we need to verify uniqueness collision risks; we may need a salted hash tied to our tenancy.
[00:05:32] Liam: We can support tenancy-salted hashing to avoid cross-customer collisions.
[00:05:36] Sara: Procurement again: does the amendment include IP/ownership language for prompts and outputs? Our legal wants explicit language that customer retains rights.
[00:05:45] Maya: Yes, standard clause: customer retains rights to prompts and outputs; Redwood has no claim. We'll include redlines.
[00:05:50] Jon: Anything on model rollouts? We will want canary deploys and automatic fallback to previous model on regressions.
[00:05:57] Liam: Our rollout tooling supports canary and A/B with auto-rollbacks on quality regressions tied to eval sets. We'll show the console flow in the pilot.
[00:06:05] Priya: For billing: can you show an example invoice for a blended month where we have reserved + burst usage? Finance likes examples.
[00:06:12] Maya: We'll attach a sample invoice and a blended cost calc in the pricing worksheet.
[00:06:16] Sara: Great.
[00:06:18] Maya: Ok quick recap and timeline — we'll: 1) send pricing worksheet and contract amendment draft by Monday 12/13, 2) run and share bench results by 12/17, 3) security artifacts and SSO metadata exchange, 4) target pilot kickoff first week of January for EU VPC. Anything missing?
[00:06:34] Priya: That covers it. Also share SOC2 and security pack.
[00:06:38] Jon: And include expected cold-start numbers for the long-context models — we need to baseline tokenization and KV warmups.
[00:06:45] Liam: We'll include cold-start and warm-up curves in the benchmark report.
[00:06:49] Maya: Perfect. Last question — competitors: I know you mentioned Anthropic internally, are you testing others?
[00:06:56] Priya: We're doing a small eval bench with Anthropic for latency, and also looking at self-hosted for the doc-summarization workload. Still leaning toward your managed approach for the chat endpoint though.
[00:07:07] Maya: Good to hear.
[00:07:09] Sara: Procurement note — we'll need Redwood's insurance cert for legal review; can you share that?
[00:07:14] Maya: Yes, I'll include certs in the security packet.
[00:07:18] Priya: Cool. Anything else from your side?
[00:07:21] Liam: No, I think we have the action items.
[00:07:24] Maya: Awesome thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the worksheet and schedule.
[00:07:29] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:07:31] (meeting ends)

Recap (auto):
- Customer to run EU private VPC pilot with reserved capacity for latency-sensitive workload; timeline 4–6 weeks to onboard after network/KMS confirmation.
- Redwood to provide a 12-month reserved pricing worksheet, contract amendment with step-down provisions, security artifacts (SOC2, encryption docs), and run a 24-hour benchmark matrix including cache/no-cache and cold-start measurements.
